summary: Phase 3 Rework acceptance passes at 024cfdf9. Provenance: git rev-parse HEAD gives 024cfdf9250384667142481856d17eebca91cb15, the audited HEAD, and it is current. phase_base_sha b78fdde1 resolves. All gates re-run live: check-rework.sh exits 0 with === Total: 41 checks (PASS=41, FAIL=0) ===; adversarial-p3.sh exits 0 with the committed tree at 41/41, the control fixture at 41/41, and every probe (01 to 08) caught or passing as designed; ls -l lists both fresh mill shots (1185352 and 1288124 bytes); sha256sum prints 32a41dc0... and 0543e6a6..., equal to rework-mill.json; git diff --exit-code b78fdde1..HEAD -- docs/fantasy-world-scene-blueprints.tsv assets/watermill.ts is empty. The rework is the planned smallest change: scenes/maps/mill.ts line 125 adds yaw: -65 to the watermill place and nothing else. The rerate is independent: kimi 7.5, critical false, audited head 304a75d6 descends from the rework commit 7619c491, and kimi differs from the original maker family (Anthropic Sonnet) and the rework maker family (hy). The stop rule holds: three labeled ratings (MAPS 7.0, Judge 5.5, Rerate 7.5), no fourth rating, no follow-up row. The TSV stays a Phase 4 task. Prerequisite coverage: Review A and Review C pass at cddadba3, and every commit between cddadba3 and the audited HEAD (6cc6f91f, fa85bb2a, 024cfdf9) touches only measure/runs/ test and evidence files, so both reviews still cover the implementation content; fa85bb2a grew the checker from 39 to 41 checks to close ADV-5 and ADV-6, and the adversarial re-audit plus this rerun prove the two new checks fire. Review B is not applicable per test-strategy section 10. UX browser review: a separate run is not required; the kimi rerate judge is itself the visual check of the two fresh shots, and no other vision route exists. Five nonblocking items carry to Phase 4; none blocks Phase 3.

The operative claim (the checker exits 0) matches reality and the gate is now strictly stronger: this audit re-ran it live at 41/41. The plan also names no citation for the ADV-5/ADV-6 closure. Route: when Phase 4 edits plan.md, refresh the quote to 41 and add one line citing fa85bb2a. Echo of review-a F1 scope and review-c evidence line 24.

N2 [Nit] plan Gate block still names bathhouse paths (measure/tracks/asset_scenes_civic_20260928/plan.md:99-101) although the reworked slug is mill. The plan's own Green evidence text (plan.md:112-113) names the correct mill gate, and both mill shots verify live: sizes 1185352 and 1288124 bytes, sha256 equal to rework-mill.json, last commit 7619c491. The Gate block is strategy template residue written before the below-bar map was known. Route: Phase 4 points the Gate block at the reworked slug. Carried from review-a F1.

N3 [Nit, carried, required Phase 4 verification] generator drift (scripts/design-mill.mjs:25 versus scenes/maps/mill.ts:125): the generator still writes put('watermill', 2.2, -3.4) with no yaw while the committed mill.ts carries yaw: -65, and the mill.ts header says 'GENERATED by scripts/design-mill.mjs - edit the generator, not this file'. A future generator run silently drops the rework and regenerates the edge-on wheel. Not a Phase 3 blocker: plan.md line 81 allows editing scenes/maps/<slug>.ts directly, the checker verifies the rework commit touched the source (adversarial probe 01 proves the check fires), and the drift is disclosed in green-p3.log lines 73-74, review-a F2, and review-c F2. The brief states Phase 4 Green fixes the generator and proves mill.ts byte-identical. This acceptance carries that proof as a required Phase 4 item so the accepted state stays durable.

N4 [Nit] check-review.sh is now permanently red on the mill accepted state: this audit re-ran it live, exit 1 with === Total: 34 checks (PASS=33, FAIL=1) === and the single FAIL 'P2-d row for mill holds state cell [accepted], want [rated]', exactly as plan.md lines 114-118 record. By design, so Phase 3 needs no fix. Phase 4 closeout must carry the one-line note so a full phase-checker sweep at closeout is not misread as a regression. Carried from review-a F4.

N5 [Nit] test-strategy freshness wording drift (measure/tracks/asset_scenes_civic_20260928/test-strategy.md:154 versus check-rework.sh:19-21): the strategy says each shot has 'an mtime newer than the rework', while the checker proves recency with git log because a checkout resets mtime. The falsifier still holds: probe 01 and the Review A fixture M1 both fail a shot committed before the rework commit. A strategy wording fix would remove the drift; same class as the open F8 spec item. Carried from review-a F3.

The allowed test-only commits are 6cc6f91f, fa85bb2a, and 024cfdf9. fa85bb2a grew the checker by two checks; the adversarial re-audit committed at 024cfdf9 and this audit's own rerun prove both new checks fire and the committed tree passes 41/41.

Adversarial chain: the first run at cddadba3 (adversarial-p3-cddadba.json, status pass) found two checker gaps with no live instance, routed as ADV-5 and ADV-6: the checker did not verify the rework commit touched its source_paths, and did not verify the rerate audited_head descended from the rework commit. Red closed both in fa85bb2a (test-only: check-rework.sh +24 lines, red-p3.log +21 lines). The re-audit (adversarial-p3-fa85bb2.json, status pass, committed in 024cfdf9) proves both closures with exact FAIL lines, and this audit re-ran adversarial-p3.sh at 024cfdf9 with the same result: exit 0, every probe caught.

Review B applicability: not applicable per test-strategy section 10 line 256 (no product code beyond the one planned map line, no repository network call, no secret, no login, no write outside owned paths). Confirmed: the phase diff adds no script that reads environment secrets.

UX browser decision: a separate UX browser review is not required for Phase 3. The test-strategy section 10 UX scope is visual only: 'look at the 30 three-quarter and top shots and at every fresh rework shot'. The only fresh rework shots are the two mill PNGs, and the independent kimi vision judge performed exactly that look as part of the rerate: rerate-mill.log lines 8-9 record the inputs (mill.md brief, mill.jpg mockup, mill-3q.png, mill-top.png), lines 11-29 record the visual findings, and the result block names role 'ux-browser-review (independent map judge, rerate)' with the four image paths as evidence. Kimi differs from both maker families. No other vision route exists: the claude family is excluded as the original maker family, and this audit confirmed locally that the acceptance route cannot read images (the read of mill-3q.png returned 'this model does not support image input'). A separate UX review would therefore use the same kimi route and add no independence over the rerate. Phase 2 already holds a separate UX spot check (ux-browser-review-p2-0aed743.json) covering the wider 30-map sample, and the maker-side crop check in green-p3.log lines 37-40 corroborates the wheel reading. The binding visual proof of Phase 3 is the independent rerate of the actual fresh PNGs.
